complete_examples.text: The rail is modelled as an infinite Euler beam discretely supported by the fastener system, which is generally represented by a series of spring-dashpot elements.
Considering the high integrity of the concrete slab and the supporting layer, these two components are equivalent to one single concrete layer which is also simulated as an infinite Euler beam.
The rail can be represented as an Euler beam with vertical, lateral and torsional motions, which is sufficient for analyzing train-induced dynamic responses in the tunnel-soil system.
This is because modeling the rail as an Euler beam fail to capture the actual high-frequency vibrations in the rail.
